MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 at p = 5.65×10⁻⁹, hitting the identical five compounds: galactitol (C01697), galactinol (C01235), glycerol (C00116), myo-inositol (C00137), and sucrose (C00089). The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm scored galactose metabolism rank 4 (p = 0.0065), with 12 of 13 pathway members matched by mass-space inference, adding β-D-glucose (C00221) as an additional hit that did not surface in the annotation-limited ORA tools. The consistent five-metabolite core maps to the Leloir pathway: sucrose enters as an external galactose source; galactinol serves as the galactosyl donor for raffinose-family oligosaccharide biosynthesis; galactitol is the aldose-reductase product of galactose; myo-inositol and glycerol are interconnected hub metabolites linking galactose catabolism to membrane phospholipid remodelling. RaMP separately captured glycerol and myo-inositol driving glycerophospholipid biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1483206, FDR 5.6×10⁻⁴) and myo-inositol driving phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (mummichog, rank 3), suggesting a secondary perturbation of lipid signalling. Detomidine (KEGG:C07450) and methimazole (C07190) were excluded from the galactose consensus: detomidine is a veterinary imidazole sedative with a connectivity-conflict InChIKey relative to human dexmedetomidine, and methimazole was unresolvable to ChEBI, indicating these are likely off-target or species-specific hits that do not belong to the curated human metabolic network.
